Subject: Data residency confirmation for EU deployment

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As part of our procurement checklist we need a short architecture overview (one deck) that clearly calls out: region guarantees, VPC/private connect options, KMS/CMK handling in the EU region, and an operational runbook for connecting via our transit VPC.

High level asks:
- A single-slide summary saying whether customer data can be guaranteed to remain in EU-hosted nodes (we will need regions and cloud provider names).
- A connectivity runbook showing private link / peering options and any firewall/port requirements.
- Any limitations for cache/replication or backup retention that could move data outside EU.

Can you share a deck + runbook by EOD next Friday (Apr 17)? Legal copied for visibility — they may have follow-ups on KMS and sub-processor list.

Best,
Sara

Karthik / Monica — attached is the first pass of the architecture deck and the EU VPC topology diagram. Highlights included on the opening slide:
- Data residency statement: Orbital tenant can be pinned to EU regions (AWS eu-west-1, GCP europe-west4). Customer data storage and primary inference nodes will run in those regions.
- KMS model: we support both Redwood-managed keys (we can restrict to EU-managed KMS instances) and customer-supplied CMKs via external KMS integration.
- Replication: by default we do not replicate inference logs or long-term backups to other regions; we call out where multi-region replication might be required (optional add-on).

Attachments referenced: [attachment: redwood-architecture-deck-v3.pptx (1.8 MB)], [attachment: vpc-topology-eu-diagram.png (420 KB)]

- Legal asked earlier about sub-processors; will forward the current sub-processor list once Karthik confirms.

Thanks — feedback welcome.

Hi Sara / Legal — attaching the final package per your checklist. Contents:
- redwood-architecture-deck-v3.pptx — includes the explicit data residency slide and the KMS flow for EU-hosted customer keys.
- private-connect-runbook-v1.pdf — step-by-step options: Transit VPC peering, DirectConnect/ExpressRoute private link, IP allowlist and firewall ports, expected handoff points for Orbital network team.
- vpc-topology-eu-diagram.png — network diagram used in the runbook.

Attachment stubs: [attachment: private-connect-runbook-v1.pdf (420 KB)], [attachment: redwood-architecture-deck-v3.pptx (1.8 MB)], [attachment: vpc-topology-eu-diagram.png (420 KB)]

Key callouts (summary):
- Residency guarantee: Redwood can provision the Orbital tenant on EU-only compute/storage nodes. We will not intentionally egress customer data outside EU except for controlled telemetry/metrics which can be toggled off; this is documented in slide 3.
- KMS options: Customer can bring CMKs (we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS integrations) — with CMKs, key material never leaves the configured KMS region.
- Failover: cross-region failover is optional and requires an explicit change order; default configuration keeps primary services in EU.

Next steps:
1) If Legal is satisfied, we'll share the sub-processor list and an updated Addendum for the data processing agreement.
2) If Orbital wants a dry-run private-connect test, propose Apr 28 for network handoff/testing.
